question: Why can insertion order damage the performance of a binary search tree, and what bounded-height alternative is mentioned?

plan.raw: O1|S16,S19,S20,S21|The insertion order can damage the performance of a binary search tree because arbitrary insertions may lead to degeneracy, causing the tree to degrade into a singly linked list, which results in linear time complexity. A bounded-height alternative mentioned is self-balancing variants of BSTs, which bound the worst-case lookup complexity to that of the binary logarithm.
